correctness.rationale: The exact normalizations were recovered from RESULT.md: g(t)=t exp(-pi t^2), ab=1/2, and H_a=a(|Z_a g(x,w)|^2+|Z_a g(x,w-b)|^2). Gaussian derivative series converge locally uniformly. Odd parity at w=0 and b eliminates even-order Zak Taylor terms, so H has the diagonal quadratic form X u^2+Y v^2 plus quartic order. Poisson summation gives A_0=(2pi/a^3)sum_{k in Z}k^2 exp(-pi k^2/a^2)>0, and B_0=-2pi a^2 sum n^2 exp(-pi a^2 n^2)<0; hence both axes strictly positive. Comparing even/odd half-lattice Gaussian sums yields X(a)=Y(1/(2a)) and vice versa. Half-integer dual terms yield X~pi^2 a^-5 exp(-pi/(2a^2)), Y~a^-1 as a->0; n=0 and n=±1 yield X~2a,Y~32pi^2 a^5 exp(-2pi a^2) as a->infinity. Positive quadratic polar integration gives each local area =pi epsilon/sqrt(XY)+O_a(epsilon^2), fixed a, near exactly the two specified zero points. Separate 45-digit direct Gaussian sums at a=0.4,0.7,1.3 confirmed X/Y Fourier duality better than 1e-35. No global zero census or uniform joint a/epsilon bound claimed.
